rawReview.evidence: The core setup uses RAW combat facts: `.references/srd-5.2.1/Playing-the-Game.md`, “Combat” → “Initiative,” permits one Initiative roll for each group of identical monsters; “Playing on a Grid,” “Movement and Position,” and “Cover” support the square scale, difficult terrain, occupied spaces, walls, and cover. The scenario's rule that player-controlled creatures win remaining Initiative ties is a synthetic override: the same Initiative passage assigns a monster–player-character tie to the GM. `.references/srd-5.2.1/Rules-Glossary.md`, “Bright Light,” “Darkvision,” “Dash [Action],” “Disengage [Action],” “Dodge [Action],” “Opportunity Attacks,” and “Utilize [Action]” support the stated baseline mechanics. `.references/srd-5.2.1/Equipment.md`, “Shield,” “Two-Handed,” “Tinderbox,” and “Torch” support the equipment and illumination concepts. The printed statistics and average HP are supplied by `.references/srd-5.2.1/Monsters/Monsters-C-D.md`, “Commoner”; `.references/srd-5.2.1/Monsters/Monsters-P-S.md`, “Skeletons” → “Skeleton”; `.references/srd-5.2.1/Monsters/Monsters-T-Z.md`, “Zombies” → “Zombie”; and `.references/srd-5.2.1/Animals.md`, “Wolf.” The unarmed Commoner is a visible stat-block modification, while `.references/srd-5.2.1/Monsters/Overview.md`, “Gear” → “Equipping a Monster with Other Items,” leaves monster equipment to the GM. The Initiative override, lift, brazier actions, scripted control, final victory triggers, and immediate roster removal are explicit synthetic table rules rather than hidden RAW claims; `ASSUMPTIONS.md`, “A33: Mid-combat roster and initiative changes are caller decisions,” supports making departure/removal caller-defined. No irreconcilable internal contradiction is evident.
rawReview.critique: The scenario is not yet fully executable without additional explicit Table Decisions. Define (1) how multiclass characters count toward “one Cleric,” “one Rogue,” and “one Barbarian or Fighter,” including whether one adventurer may satisfy multiple requirements; (2) what “qualified” means for the light carrier, what light source begins exposed, and whether “the exposed-light carrier” remains a fixed identity after the light is extinguished, dropped, transferred, or supplemented; and (3) whether “printed average Hit Points” applies only to stat-block creatures, plus the adventurers’ starting current HP and expendable-resource state. Close the defender script’s unresolved branches: what Zombies do when holding without an adjacent target; how post-crossing Zombies choose between spaces adjacent to the Commoner and P10; what a withdrawing Wolf does when no conscious Zombie exists; what “safe route,” “closest,” “can reach without Dashing,” “movement could reach the lift entrance,” and “able to reach the chain” mean; which enemy a Skeleton moves to obtain a ranged attack against, whether it Dashes when no firing position is reachable this turn, and what cover direction its post-crossing position must address; and how remaining ties are resolved. Also prioritize the post-departure instructions to pursue adventurers versus occupy A6/A7. Finally, specify lift occupancy for Tiny or Large creatures and additional creatures such as familiars or summons, and define when the continuation ends for creatures temporarily unable to act. RAW supplies no answers to those scenario-specific branches, and `ASSUMPTIONS.md` does not settle them.

policyReview.evidence: The artifact uses canonical SRD identities and standard rules terminology (including Commoner, Skeleton, Zombie, Wolf, the named classes, Pack Tactics, actions, cover, light, movement, and initiative) plus generic scenario elements such as a mine, lift, walls, pillars, bins, and braziers. It contains no identifiable PHB+ record names, ids, slugs, headings, page references, source mappings, or protected examples, and its map, objectives, setup, behavioral procedures, ordering, and presentation read as independently authored scenario expression rather than recognizable PHB+ prose or sequencing.
